papers.title: The compositional nature of the human alpha rhythm
papers.abstract: Resting-state brain activity is dominated by oscillations in the alpha band (8-13 Hz). The dominant frequency within this band, the individual alpha peak frequency (IAPF), has been widely used as a global marker of inter-individual variability in perceptual and cognitive functions, as well as clinical phenotypes. However, the traditional approach implicitly assumes a single oscillatory rhythm varying along a parametric continuum. Here, we analyzed resting-state EEG data from more than 2000 participants across multiple independent datasets using unsupervised spectral decomposition methods. We identify three distinct and highly stable alpha components, or archetypes, that jointly and compositionally determine the IAPF. These components exhibit dissociable age-related trajectories as well as distinct scalp topographies and cortical sources. Together, these findings indicate that individual differences in alpha activity do not reflect variation along a single frequency dimension, but rather differences in the relative contribution of discrete alpha generators. These results call for a reevaluation of many reported associations between alpha frequency, brain function, and clinical phenotypes, and suggest that estimates of alpha-component expression may provide more precise and informative biomarkers than conventional global IAPF measures.

ai.summary: Using resting-state EEG from over 2000 participants and unsupervised spectral decomposition, the authors identified three stable, dissociable alpha-band components that compositionally determine the individual alpha peak frequency, each with distinct age trajectories, scalp topographies, and cortical sources. The findings indicate that inter-individual alpha variability reflects relative contributions of discrete alpha generators rather than a single frequency continuum, arguing for component-expression markers over global IAPF.

papers.title: A synchronized dual-scale platform combining flexible micro-ECoG and skull-screw EEG reveals frequency-dependent cortex-to-skull spectral gain in awake mice.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is the most scalable window onto brain dynamics, yet how cortical activity is transformed before reaching extracranial electrodes has largely been inferred from forward models rather than directly measured. We built a dual-scale sensing platform in awake mice that records a 16-channel flexible micro-electrocorticography (micro-ECoG) array and five skull-screw EEG electrodes on a single 30-kHz clock, enabling sample-aligned comparison of cortical and skull-level signals. Across 115 simultaneously recorded ECoG-EEG pairs from three mice, cortex-to-skull spectral gain was not frequency-flat but increased with frequency following a power law, indicating that skull EEG relatively preserves high-frequency cortical activity rather than acting as a simple low-pass copy. This gain was also non-stationary: it shifted across blocks of a fixed-order auditory protocol and was not explained by measured video motion, whereas trial-matched cross-scale coherence depended on the reference transform. With channel number equalized, micro-ECoG retained a larger unique spatial component than skull EEG. These results convert the cortex-to-skull relationship from a static modeling assumption into a measurable, frequency- and state-dependent quantity. For neural sensing, they provide an empirical calibration target for choosing electrode scale, reference, and analysis band and for validating EEG forward models and EEG-to-intracranial translation. More broadly, they indicate that noninvasive biomarkers and brain-computer interface features, particularly in high-frequency bands, should be interpreted through frequency- and state-aware cortex-to-skull mappings.

papers.title: Breathing-evoked potentials in humans during wakefulness and sleep.
papers.abstract: Breathing modulates cortical activities and cognitive functions, but the neurophysiological basis of the brain-breathing relationship is incompletely understood. We aimed to determine whether breathing at rest evokes scalp EEG-detectable potentials (as inspiratory occlusions do in the respiratory-related evoked potential model), whether these signatures persist during sleep and whether they are linked to sleep-organizing processes. We examined recordings from 729 participants in the Cleveland Family Study to identify cortical activity time-locked to inspiration during wakefulness and sleep, with a median of 7871 respiratory cycles analysed per participant. Breathing-related cortical responses were assessed in the time and frequency domains. Quiet breathing evoked a reproducible sequence of cortical potentials during wakefulness, including a pre-inspiratory component ∼300 ms before inspiration and several post-inspiratory peaks ≤3 s after. These responses persisted during non-rapid eye movement stages 2 and 3 (N2 and N3) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, in which they showed simplified morphology resembling K-complexes and co-occurred with increased spindle-range activity. The pattern was present irrespective of body mass index and was qualitatively unchanged in the 203 participants free of sleep-disordered breathing, arguing against obesity or sleep apnoea as its origin. Scalp EEG can detect breathing-evoked potentials during quiet breathing in awake humans. These potentials persist during sleep with a morphology that resembles cortical activities previously associated with sleep stabilization. Further studies are needed to determine the physiological and clinical significance of these observations in health and disease. KEY POINTS: Spontaneous breathing at rest evokes reproducible breathing-related cortical potentials detectable with scalp EEG. These potentials persist during sleep. They are associated with time-locked modulation of cortical oscillatory activity.

papers.title: Coordinated Drift of Image Representations in Human EEG
papers.abstract: Sensory representations drift over time in many animal systems, but evidence in humans remains limited. Moreover, how perception remains stable despite representational drift remains unclear. Here, we used THINGS-EEG2, a dataset with multiple sessions of repeated presentations of natural images, to test whether image-evoked EEG responses drift across recording sessions and whether this drift is geometrically constrained. We found that image-specific EEG response patterns drifted in a manner that was coordinated across channels and concentrated along dimensions that encoded image identity. Although this impaired cross-session decoding accuracy on average, its effects were heterogeneous with some image pairs becoming harder to distinguish and others becoming more separable. Critically, global distance statistics and the dimensionality of the image response space were preserved across sessions. Simulations show that downstream Hebbian networks can adapt faster to structured drift that preserves dimensionality than when drift is unstructured. These findings suggest that human sensory representations can change over time while remaining amenable to rapid compensation via unsupervised learning mechanisms.

papers.title: Learning discriminative time-frequency representations for EEG segment-level seizure-state classification with channel selection.
papers.abstract: AbstractElectroencephalography (EEG)-based seizure monitoring supports the diagnosis andmanagement of epilepsy; however, high-dimensional multichannel EEG recordings imposesubstantial computational burden and limit suitability for portable monitoring systems.This paper proposes a reduced-channel framework for segment-level classification of EEGinto ictal, preictal and interictal states. It integrates attention-guided EEG channelselection, high-resolution time-frequency analysis via the Time ReassignedMultiSynchroSqueezing Transform (TMSST) and Concentration of Frequency and Time(ConceFT), and a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM classifier. The framework is evaluated on theCHB-MIT and Siena Scalp EEG databases under two complementary protocols: astratified 70/30 holdout split and rigorous Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validationto assess subject independent generalization. Under holdout evaluation using a single EEGchannel, the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 99.28 ± 0.63%, sensitivity of99.18%, specificity of 99.64%, and MCC of 0.97 on CHB-MIT, and an accuracy of98.75 ± 0.74%, sensitivity of 98.77%, specificity of 99.38%, and MCC(Matthews correlationcoefficients) of 0.97 on Siena. LOSO cross-validation demonstrates subject independentgeneralization, exceeding 91% accuracy on both databases. These results demonstrate thatthe framework achieves an effective balance among segment-level classification accuracy,computational efficiency and reduced-channel operation. Moreover, applicability forportable and wearable EEG-based seizure-state monitoring applications is investigated.

With a single EEG channel it reached 99.28% accuracy on CHB-MIT and 98.75% on Siena under holdout evaluation, and exceeded 91% accuracy on both databases under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.

papers.title: A canonical microcircuit for estimating Excitation/Inhibition (E/I) balance.
papers.abstract: Excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance is crucial for maintaining healthy brain function and can be disrupted in various neurological and psychiatric disorders. Despite its importance, there are few tools to study E/I balance non-invasively in humans. Here, we propose a canonical microcircuit model to estimate E/I balance from non-invasive magnetoencephalography (MEG), electroencephalography (EEG) or optically pumped magnetometers (OPM) recordings by parameterising global pyramidal and inhibitory cell excitability. We first establish that E/I parameters are identifiable and recoverable. We then explore the effects of these new parameters and their interaction with other parameters in a series of simulations. To highlight the clinical relevance of this new model, we simulate changes in E/I balance and their impact on event-related potentials (ERPs) derived from paired-click, passive and active oddball paradigms, which are among the most robust clinical biomarkers of schizophrenia. Our simulations show that a loss of pyramidal cell excitability can explain reduced ERP amplitudes across all three paradigms, mirroring empirical findings in schizophrenia. This method may serve as a computational assay for estimating synaptopathy and E/I balance from non-invasive electrophysiological recordings across various clinical conditions thereby advancing efforts to develop personalised interventions to restore E/I balance.

papers.title: Style transfer mapping with ensemble learning for cross-subject EEG-based neuropsychiatric disease recognition.
papers.abstract: Cross-subject electroencephalogram (EEG) recognition remains a fundamental challenge because large inter-subject variability causes severe distribution shifts that substantially degrade the generalization ability of existing learning models. Most existing transfer learning methods attempt to align global feature distributions but often overlook subject-specific structural variations, resulting in unstable adaptation under limited calibration data. To address this problem, we propose a Prototype-Consistent Style Transfer Mapping (PC-STM) framework for cross-subject neuropsychiatric disease recognition. Unlike conventional domain adaptation methods, the proposed framework models subject discrepancy as a prototype-guided style transformation that explicitly aligns target representations with class-consistent source prototypes while preserving discriminative structures. Specifically, a multi-source prototype construction strategy is introduced to characterize representative class distributions, followed by a confidence-aware transductive semi-supervised style transfer module that iteratively refines transformation parameters using labeled calibration samples and unlabeled evaluation samples. Furthermore, a reliability-aware ensemble learning strategy dynamically aggregates multiple subject-specific classifiers according to their calibration consistency, thereby improving robustness against heterogeneous subject distributions. Experiments on two public EEG datasets covering major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease show stable performance under the evaluated leave-one-pair-out protocol. The calibration labels are inherited from the public dataset cohorts or task conditions, and the study does not constitute prospective clinical diagnostic validation. Beyond the evaluated EEG tasks, prototype-guided style transfer may provide a basis for future investigation of other limited-supervision recognition problems.

papers.title: Digital System Physiology: Integrating Mechanistic Models, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins.
papers.abstract: A measurement tells us something about physiology only when a model interprets it, and only when that model keeps the features that matter: organization across scales, feedback, adaptation, and coupling between organs. We use the term digital system physiology for a current version of systems physiology that links many kinds of measurement, mechanistic computation, and artificial intelligence with a clear method for reasoning from data to conclusions and a preset rule for updating. Cardiac electrophysiology is the most developed clinical example. Cardiorenal, metabolic, pulmonary, and neural models are useful but less mature. In all of these areas, the evidence is stronger for mechanistic insight, individualized simulation, and early clinical feasibility than for better patient outcomes. We separate how well a model predicts from how well it explains, and we propose working criteria in which prediction and being built to inform a decision define a twin, with the cadence of updating set by the clinical question rather than by a fixed rule. Progress from here will depend on tracking each patient's state over time, coupling organs together only where it helps, stating uncertainty openly, testing models on data they were not built from, and gathering prospective evidence that matches the intended use.

papers.title: Post-intervention high-beta synchronization tracks stable-manifold alignment during stick-balancing learning
papers.abstract: Learning to stabilize an unstable object may depend not only on the accuracy of active corrective interventions but also on when to suspend intervention and allow the object's intrinsic dynamics to evolve. We investigated learning-related changes in control dynamics and associated beta-band electroencephalographic (EEG) activity during virtual stick balancing. Ten healthy young adults practiced stabilizing a virtual inverted pendulum with a joystick over two consecutive days; scalp EEG was recorded from seven participants. For each control cycle, control quality was quantified as the distance (dist) between the pendulum state at the end of each active intervention phase and the stable manifold of the control-OFF subsystem. With practice, balance duration increased, dist decreased, and the proportion of time without active intervention increased. Time-frequency responses stratified by control quality showed that post-intervention high-beta event-related synchronization was most prominent in cycles with the smallest dist. Single-cycle linear mixed-effects models further revealed an inverse association between post-intervention high-beta power and dist after accounting for intervention magnitude and movement direction, as well as trial progress where applicable. This relationship was evident in both the initial Control and final Skilled task datasets. These findings indicate that stick-balancing practice improves the ability to terminate active intervention near the stable manifold and suggest that post-intervention high-beta synchronization tracks the quality of the transition from active correction to the intrinsic dynamics of the control-OFF subsystem.

papers.title: BTBD9-driven IMPDH2 ubiquitination governs sleep homeostasis by gating adenosine metabolism in the basal forebrain.
papers.abstract: BTB domain containing 9 (BTBD9) is among the most reproducible genetic risk factors for sleep-related disorders, yet its molecular function in sleep regulation remains unclear. Here, we aimed to define the downstream substrate, core brain region, and molecular mechanism through which BTBD9 regulates sleep-wake homeostasis. Population-scale genomic and brain expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) datasets were integrated to infer the direction of BTBD9-associated genetic risk in sleep-related traits. Basal forebrain-specific neuronal manipulation of Btbd9 was combined with electroencephalography/electromyography (EEG/EMG)-based sleep analysis and fiberphotomerty to define the relevant brain locus and functional output. Ubiquitinomics, protein interaction, ubiquitination, and enzymatic assays were used to identify BTBD9-regulated substrates and determine how BTBD9-dependent modification affects metabolic enzyme activity. Basal forebrain-specific genetic disruption, receptor pharmacology, and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-delivered interfering peptides were further applied to test pathway necessity and reversibility in vivo. human genetic analyses showed that BTBD9 variants associated with higher expression predicted a pro-arousal tendency. Consistently, neuron-specific deletion of Btbd9 in the mouse basal forebrain increased non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and extracellular adenosine levels. Mechanistically, IMPDH2, the rate-limiting enzyme in de novo purine biosynthesis, was identified as a substrate of the Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase 3 (CRL3)BTBD9 ubiquitin ligase. BTBD9-mediated ubiquitination at IMPDH2 lysine 195 (K195) relieved guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-dependent allosteric inhibition, thereby limiting adenosine accumulation and sleep pressure. Basal forebrain neuronal knockout of Impdh2 recapitulated the sleep-promoting effect of Btbd9 deletion, whereas adenosine A1 receptor (A1R) blockade attenuated this phenotype. AAV-delivered interfering peptides targeting the BTBD9-IMPDH2 interaction reduced IMPDH2 ubiquitination, elevated adenosine levels, increased NREM sleep, and rescued BTBD9 overexpression-induced abnormal wakefulness in vivo. These findings identify a BTBD9-IMPDH2-adenosine pathway that links human genetic risk to basal forebrain control of sleep homeostasis. By defining BTBD9 as a molecular regulator of purine metabolism, this study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding and potentially targeting BTBD9-related sleep dysregulation.

papers.title: Magnetoencephalography in Parkinson's disease: diagnostic potential and barriers to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder with motor and nonmotor manifestations. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, and validated markers of early disease and subsequent progression are still needed. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures neuronal magnetic fields with millisecond temporal resolution and provides a means of characterizing cortical dysfunction. This narrative review critically synthesizes MEG evidence on periodic and aperiodic spectral activity, functional connectivity, network topology, and individual brain fingerprinting, with emphasis on diagnostic relevance and barriers to clinical translation. Recurring findings include spectral slowing and cognitive-network disruption, whereas resting β power, burst dynamics, and coupling depend on clinical phenotype, treatment state, and analytical choices. Evidence from electroencephalogram (EEG), functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and invasive recordings is distinguished from direct MEG findings. Internally validated classification of established PD and healthy controls is promising, but does not establish performance in prodromal disease or clinically uncertain parkinsonism. Optically pumped magnetometers may improve recording flexibility while retaining requirements for environmental interference control. Prospective clinical cohorts, standardized acquisition and analysis, reproducibility studies, independent validation, and comparison with clinical assessment are needed to establish incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility.

papers.title: Individualized intraoperative BIS targeting based on preoperative BIS values in the awake state: a review and strategy prospect for preventing postoperative delirium in older patients.
papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication in older surgical patients and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring is widely used to guide intraoperative depth of anesthesia. However, the conventional strategy of maintaining a uniform BIS target range may not adequately account for interindividual differences in preoperative brain function, particularly in older adults with reduced neural reserve. This narrative review integrates evidence from three complementary domains: 1) clinical studies evaluating the association between preoperative resting BIS values in the awake state and the risk of POD; 2) mechanistic and clinical evidence linking excessive anesthetic depth, particularly electroencephalographic burst suppression, to POD; 3) interventional trials assessing the effect of intraoperative BIS-guided anesthesia management on delirium outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that a lower preoperative resting BIS value in the awake state is potentially independently associated with an increased risk of POD in older patients. Intraoperative BIS-guided anesthesia has been shown to reduce exposure to deep anesthesia and EEG burst suppression, which are consistently linked to higher delirium incidence. These findings suggest that patients with preoperatively identified brain vulnerability may benefit from higher individualized intraoperative BIS targets, rather than a fixed universal range. Integrating preoperative resting BIS assessment into perioperative anesthesia management may enable risk stratification and support individualized regulation of anesthetic depth in older adults. When incorporated into a multimodal delirium prevention framework, this individualized approach may offer a rational pathway toward improved delirium prevention and perioperative neuroprotection in older adults, warranting validation in future prospective randomized studies.

papers.title: An EEG-fMRI Jointly Constrained Digital Twin Brain and Its Application in Alzheime's Disease
papers.abstract: Current digital twin brain (DTB) models are typically optimized using single-modality functional neuroimaging data, which restricts their ability to simulate brain dynamics across multiple spatiotemporal scales. Here, we show that a two-stage DTB (TS-DTB) modeling framework jointly constrained by functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and electroencephalography (EEG) data. Validation in both the healthy young and Alzheimer's disease (AD) cohorts demonstrates that the TS-DTB model simultaneously captures subject-specific features of multi-scale brain dynamics. In particular, the TS-DTB models of AD patients successfully recapitulate spectral-temporal signatures of cognitive decline, suggesting a model-inferred association between these deficits and simulated excitation-inhibition (E-I) imbalances. By simulating responses to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), we further reveal that acute EEG normalization in AD patients is computationally associated with putative E-I rebalancing via model-inferred synaptic reconfiguration and background suppression. Overall, these findings underscore the potential of the TS-DTB to advance the mechanistic understanding of the brain and inform personalized digital therapeutics.

papers.title: Altered network organization with shift to local processing during adaptive behaviour in multiple sclerosis.
papers.abstract: To adjust to changing environmental demands, the brain needs to organize and (re)configure mental resources in so-called task sets. Following a network perspective of cognitive functions, these processes are considered to rely on dynamic exchange of information between distant brain regions, possibly synchronized by slow-wave theta oscillations. However, few attempts have been made to describe the directional transfer of information in theta networks during behavioural adaptation. In the current study, we examined directed neural information transfer in 57 healthy individuals and 57 patients with multiple sclerosis with a focus on brain-behaviour associations during task switching. For this, we calculated behavioural switch costs and further applied an artificial neural network-based approach on neurophysiological EEG data to estimate linear and non-linear effective connectivity measures within cortical networks during task switching. Source reconstruction and connectivity analyses revealed distinct neural network architectures and communication strategies during task switching in healthy controls compared to patients with multiple sclerosis. In healthy controls, enhanced modulations of long-range fronto-parietal connectivities were associated with higher reaction time switch costs, possibly reflecting increased cognitive demands rather than adaptive processes. In contrast, patients with multiple sclerosis relied more strongly on local intra-regional modulations, which is consistent with the idea of a dysconnectivity syndrome in multiple sclerosis. Strikingly, stronger modulations in self-connectivities were associated with better accuracy measures in patients with multiple sclerosis, suggesting a compensatory mechanism to support performance. Notably, only non-linear directed connectivity measures were related to behavioural switch costs, emphasizing the importance of non-linear models for adaptive cognitive processes.

papers.title: Altered Neural Oscillatory Coupling Reveals Cognitive Control Deficits with Hierarchical Characteristics and Emotional Specificity in Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.abstract: Cognitive control deficits are a prevalent feature of major depressive disorder (MDD) and are influenced by emotional contexts. However, it remains unclear whether these deficits specifically exist at particular hierarchical levels of cognitive control and whether they are selectively exacerbated under distinct emotional contexts. Furthermore, the neural mechanisms underlying such deficits and their association with depressive symptoms remain to be further elucidated. To fill these gaps, two experiments were conducted. In Experiment 1, 54 MDDs and 41 healthy controls (HCs) performed emotional and non-emotional hierarchical cognitive control tasks. Hierarchical demands were manipulated using low- and high-abstraction rules. Based on hierarchy- and emotion-specific deficits identified in Experiment 1, Experiment 2 (34 MDDs; 28 HCs) introduced rule memory set-size manipulation to test whether the deficit generalized to other hierarchical cognitive control subprocesses. Electroencephalography and eye-tracking were simultaneously recorded. Phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) quantified cross-frequency interactions subserving cognitive control. Delta-beta PAC was selectively reduced in MDDs compared with HCs during high-abstraction conditions under negative emotional contexts, but not in low-abstraction conditions or other contexts. Under the same conditions, MDDs also failed to show the typical memory-related increase in theta-gamma PAC. Moreover, emotion regulation scores significantly mediated the pathway from PAC abnormalities to depressive severity. Our findings indicate that altered neural oscillatory coupling reveals cognitive control deficits in MDD that exhibit both hierarchical characteristics and emotional specificity. These neural abnormalities may contribute to depressive severity through maladaptive emotion regulation strategies, providing a novel biological account of the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying MDD.

papers.title: Interictal epileptic discharge > 1% associated with cognitive impairment in adult patients with epilepsy: A cross-sectional study based on dose-response relationship and discharge characteristics.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is frequently accompanied by multidomain cognitive impairment, but the quantitative contribution of interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs)-including discharge burden, vigilance state, and spatial distribution-to specific cognitive domains remains incompletely defined. This cross-sectional study aimed to examine associations between multidimensional IED parameters and domain-specific cognitive function in non-symptomatic adult epilepsy. We analyzed long-term EEG-derived IED indices during sleep and wakefulness, lateralization, focal/multifocal distribution, and frontal/temporal involvement in 114 adults with non-symptomatic epilepsy, relating these metrics to a neuropsychological battery using ANCOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. After adjustment for age, education, disease duration, seizure duration, seizure frequency, and antiepileptic drug count, a sleep IED index > 1% remained associated with lower Montreal Cognitive Assessment, associative learning, and verbal fluency scores versus the < 1% group; Mini-Mental State Examination was borderline and visual recognition did not survive FDR. Compared with no discharge, sleep > 1% showed lower Digit Symbol and verbal fluency scores only at uncorrected significance. For wakefulness, no significant graded association emerged between < 1% and > 1% groups; versus no discharge, wake > 1% showed lower Digit Symbol and verbal fluency scores at uncorrected level only. Discharges during both sleep and wakefulness were associated with lower backward digit span than sleep-only discharges, with a trend after FDR. Lateralization and focal/multifocal distribution were not significantly associated after FDR. Frontal IEDs were associated with lower verbal fluency and attention-related scores versus no discharge, but direct regional contrasts were nonsignificant and limited by small subgroups. A sleep IED index > 1% may represent a candidate electrophysiological marker of domain-specific cognitive vulnerability, whereas a wakefulness threshold and clear regional specificity were not definitively established. These findings support vigilance-state-aware quantification of IED burden while highlighting the need for larger longitudinal studies with detailed medication profiling.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approaches in deep learning-driven EEG analysis for the diagnosis of neurological diseases. It includes recent advances in deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), hybrid configurations, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Large Language Models (LLM), autoencoders, and transformer-based models, with a focus on their capacity to model spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal dynamics in EEG signals. This is applicable in diagnosing major neurological disorders such as Epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease (AD), Encephalopathy, Parkinson's disease (PD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), sleep disorders, and developmental brain disorders. Furthermore, we discuss essential preprocessing strategies and denoising techniques, showing how removing biological artifacts prevents diagnostic models from confusing noise with actual signs of disease. Key challenges such as limited data availability, lack of model interpretability, inter-subject variability, and difficulty in clinical translation are identified and critically discussed. Finally, key emerging trends and future research directions are identified to support the development of clinical applications of EEG-based disease diagnostic systems.

papers.title: Disrupted Top-Down Modulation as a Mechanism of Impaired Multisensory Processing in Autistic Children.
papers.abstract: Atypical sensory processing is commonly observed in autism, particularly when integration across sensory modalities is required. The neural mechanisms underlying multisensory differences remain unclear. We recorded EEG while autistic children aged 8-13 (AU;n = 40), siblings of autistic children (SIB;n = 26), and non-autistic controls (NA;n = 36) performed a simple reaction-time task to auditory (A), visual (V), and audiovisual (AV) stimuli. Analyses targeted event-related potentials (ERPs), alpha-band event-related desynchronization (α-ERD), and long-range theta-band functional connectivity. Groups did not differ across unisensory measures, indicating comparable unisensory processing. By contrast, multisensory integration (MSI;AV-(A+V)) differed across groups: NA children showed significant ERP MSI over parieto-central sites that was absent in AU and SIB; and α-ERD MSI was significantly reduced in AU, with SIB showing an intermediate profile. Connectivity analyses revealed reduced AV fronto-parieto-occipital coupling in autistic children relative to non-autistic children, suggesting weaker large-scale coordination during multisensory processing. These results point to a multisensory-specific deficit spanning early sensory encoding, posterior α-ERD, and fronto-posterior coupling and support disrupted multisensory influences on sensory processing due to reduced multisensory attentional orienting. SIB profiles suggest inherited liability for these neural phenotypes. These results help explain well-documented behavioral MSI differences in autism by linking impaired early enhancement with attenuated top-down control of sensory cortex.

papers.title: EEG-based brain effective and functional connectivity predict PET-defined amyloid positivity in cognitively normal individuals.
papers.abstract: Early identification of amyloid-beta (Aβ) pathology is essential for timely intervention in Alzheimer's disease (AD), as Aβ accumulation precedes clinical symptoms by years. We predicted positron emission tomography (PET) -defined Aβ status in cognitively normal individuals using non-invasive resting-state dry electroencephalography (EEG). Brain effective and functional connectivity were quantified to characterize dynamic information transfer between regions. Features derived from dynamic brain connectivity were used to train machine learning models for Aβ classification. EEG-based models can predict amyloid positivity with accuracy comparable to, or in some cases exceeding, that of plasma p-tau217 and previously reported predictors based on cognitive measures, demographics, and health factors, depending on the model. Beyond near real-time Aβ inference, the framework identifies the most affected brain regions and connections associated with neurodegeneration, offering complementary information to blood-based biomarkers and supporting its potential as an affordable tool for early AD detection in primary care and population screening.

papers.title: Susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distractors in relation to visual working memory in children with and without attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder associated with increased distractibility. Previous research has reported that susceptibility to task-irrelevant visual distraction is linked with visual working memory (WM) capacity in adults. Here, we examined how neural susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distractors related to visual WM capacity in children with and without ADHD. Across two experiments, electroencephalography (EEG) signals were recorded from 146 Chinese children aged 7-15 (63 with ADHD, 23% girls; collected in 2022-2024), during which they performed visual tasks of varying difficulty with auditory distractors. The mismatch negativity (MMN) amplitude was measured as neural susceptibility to auditory distractors, and a K-score was calculated to assess visual WM capacity. In typically developing (TD) children, those with higher visual WM capacity showed less susceptibility to auditory distractors under high audiovisual competition (r = 0.494), whereas this relation reversed under low competition (r = -0.319). Conversely, in children with ADHD, lower visual WM capacity predicted higher susceptibility under both high (r = 0.442) and low competition (r = 0.326). These findings indicate that susceptibility to task-irrelevant auditory distraction is related to visual WM capacity in children, but the patterns differ between typical and atypical neurodevelopment and are modulated by audiovisual competition.

papers.title: EEG network analysis to identify cortical pathology in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify preoperative electrophysiologic biomarkers to localize the epileptogenic zone (EZ) and predict surgical outcomes in patients with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) using a graph-theoretical network analysis. We retrospectively analyzed preoperative long-term EEG data from 71 LGS patients in three subgroups: Group A (n = 23), with favorable outcomes after resective surgery (RS); Group B (n = 22), with unfavorable outcomes after RS; and Group C (n = 26), who underwent palliative surgery instead of RS. We analyzed 500-ms EEG windows centered on the point of peak phase coupling preceding interictal generalized sharp-and-slow waves. We computed two sets of biomarkers: (1) the clustering coefficient (CCE) to assess overall network connectivity, and (2) a novel 'Network Dominance Score' (the product of Betweenness Centrality, Node Out-Degree, and Node Out-Strength) to identify the putative ictogenic hub. The CCE effectively differentiate the favorable-outcome group (Group A), the unfavorable-outcome group (Group B), and the palliative surgery group (Group C) (Area Under the Curve = 0.915). The Network Dominance Score achieved 100% accuracy in correctly lateralizing the lesion for all patients in the Group A. Conversely, for the Group B, this analysis identified either bilateral or incorrectly localized hubs, demonstrating a clear correlation between our analytical findings and surgical outcomes. This graph-theoretical approach offers a promising non-invasive tool to augment conventional presurgical evaluations, improve patient selection for RS, and predict surgical outcomes in individuals with LGS.

papers.title: Neural, vascular, motor and autonomic habituation to high-intensity auditory stimulation: A multimodal characterization of the human defensive responses.
papers.abstract: The defense reflex has been extensively characterized across sensory modalities; however, the integration of electrical, neurovascular, motor, and peripheral autonomic responses involving the central and autonomic nervous systems remains poorly understood. This study investigated defensive responses to high-intensity auditory stimulation using a multimodal approach combining electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and peripheral physiological measures. Participants were exposed to twenty white-noise bursts (100 dB, 500 ms, instantaneous rise time) separated by silent intervals (50 ± 10 s), grouped into five blocks to assess initial responses and habituation. Hemodynamic responses revealed widespread activation of bilateral auditory and frontal regions following stimulus onset, with a progressive reduction in response amplitude and extension of active channels across blocks. Network analysis suggests progressive reorganization of functional connectivity between sensory and frontal regions across repeated stimulation. At the peripheral level, habituation was observed in phasic electrodermal activity, vascular indices, motor response, EEG-derived ocular activity, and parasympathetic cardiac modulation, primarily after the first block, whereas respiratory measures remained stable. Cardiac defense-like responses show a multi-temporal component structure, with habituation restricted to the late decelerative phase. Multivariate analyses revealed a structured yet partially independent organization of neural and autonomic responses to habituation. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive characterization of multisystem responses to intense auditory stimulation, highlighting selective habituation across central, neurovascular, motor, and autonomic systems, and offering new insights into how neurovascular and peripheral processes adapt to repeated auditory threats.

papers.title: Impact of hearing loss on visual selective attention: Evidence from N2pc and resting-state networks.
papers.abstract: Efficient visual attention is fundamental to environmental adaptation and social interaction. While previous studies have observed alterations in visual processing among deaf individuals, findings remain controversial regarding whether these changes stem from hearing loss (sensory compensation vs. cognitive deficit) or sign language experience. To address this issue, the present study provides task-related and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) evidence to disentangle the specific drivers of visual selective attention plasticity. A visual search task was used to examine selective attention in 95 participants (34 prelingual deaf, 27 hearing signers, and 34 hearing nonsigners). Compared to both hearing groups, deaf individuals exhibited significantly lower hit rates and diminished N2-posterior contralateral (N2pc) amplitudes. Hearing signers and nonsigners showed comparable behavioral performance, N2pc amplitudes, and resting-state network topology, whereas the deaf group was further characterized by a degraded resting-state alpha network topology, evidenced by reduced clustering coefficients, global efficiency, and weakened frontal-occipital connectivity. N2pc amplitude correlated significantly with resting-state network properties and behavioral accuracy. These results suggest that deaf individuals may suffer from an imbalance in the regulation of visual selective attention, most clearly indexed by the evoked N2pc and by intrinsic alpha-network organization, and likely linked to increased resource competition following the loss of auditory monitoring. Our findings provide neurophysiological evidence that these attentional deficits are associated with hearing loss rather than with sign-language experience, offering a new perspective for understanding the boundaries of cross-modal plasticity in the human brain.

papers.title: Prefrontal rTMS modulates dynamic expectancy processes to shape subsequent pain experience.
papers.abstract: Pain expectancy is a major determinant of pain perception, and identifying effective approaches to modulate expectancy may provide new opportunities for pain intervention. High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) has been implicated in expectancy-related pain modulation. However, it remains unclear how DLPFC-rTMS influences distinct stages of expectancy processing and how these changes relate to subsequent pain experience. Thirty-three healthy participants completed a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled crossover study. Participants received real or sham high-frequency DLPFC-rTMS and performed a pain expectancy paradigm before and after stimulation while EEG was recorded. The paradigm dissociated expectancy formation and maintenance under certain and uncertain predictive contexts. Behaviorally, DLPFC-rTMS reduced pain intensity and unpleasantness, accompanied by a reduction in expected pain, and mediation analysis identified an indirect effect through expected pain. At the neural level, DLPFC-rTMS increased contextual cue-evoked P2 responses relative to sham during expectancy formation but reduced anticipatory N1 and contingent negative variation (CNV) responses during expectancy maintenance. During pain experience, laser-evoked N1 responses showed a context-dependent pattern, with greater attenuation under uncertainty. Importantly, mediation analyses identified distinct stage-related indirect associations: stimulation-related changes in contextual P2 responses were linked to subsequent laser-evoked N1 responses, whereas changes in anticipatory CNV and anxiety were jointly associated with subsequent pain ratings. Together, these findings demonstrate that DLPFC-rTMS modulates dynamic expectancy processes across distinct stages of pain anticipation, with formation- and maintenance-related changes linked to different aspects of subsequent pain processing.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction in depression: dual-task event-related potentials and task-phase-dependent EEG functional connectivity.
papers.abstract: To investigate the neurophysiological features underlying depression-related cognitive dysfunction via dual-task event-related potential (ERP) and task-phase-dependent electroencephalography (EEG) functional connectivity analysis. Thirty patients with depression (DP group) and 30 matched healthy controls (HC group) underwent EEG recordings across pre-task resting state, face perception task (indexed by N170), face mismatch conflict monitoring task (indexed by N270), and post-task resting state. Functional connectivity was quantified using imaginary coherence (iCoh), with between-group comparisons corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR). Correlation analyses between electrophysiological metrics and clinical variables were performed in the DP group. The DP group exhibited prolonged latency and decreased amplitude of N170, prolonged latency and increased amplitude of N270, as well as task-phase-dependent multi-frequency brain network imbalances. In the DP group, longer N170 and N270 latencies were associated with more severe depressive symptoms, whereas task-phase-dependent functional connectivity abnormalities showed no significant associations with clinical variables. Depression was associated with electrophysiological abnormalities in emotional processing and conflict monitoring, as well as task-phase-dependent brain network imbalances, providing exploratory neurophysiological evidence related to depression-associated cognitive dysfunction. papers.title: Cooperative processing of visual threat across collicular pathways
papers.abstract: Rapid defensive actions require the transformation of sensory cues into appropriate motor responses. The superior colliculus is central to this transformation, containing defined cell-types that form parallel output pathways linking visual inputs to distinct behaviors. However, whether these pathways act independently or cooperate remains unclear. Here we combine cell-type-specific inhibition, large-scale electrophysiology, and functional ultrasound imaging to determine how these pathways contribute to visually evoked defensive behaviors. Inhibiting either narrow-field or wide-field neurons impaired escape to overhead visual threats, demonstrating that both pathways contribute to escape. Recordings from downstream targets revealed a compact representation in the deeper layers of the superior colliculus that selectively distinguished visual stimuli associated with escape, whereas the lateral posterior thalamus contained a broader representation of visual stimuli. The representation of visual threat in the deeper layers of the superior colliculus predicted escape initiation and vigor in freely moving animals. Across the brain, functional ultrasound imaging showed that visual stimuli recruited distinct patterns of activity that could not be explained by response magnitude alone or by the contribution of single cell-types. Together, these results reveal a cooperative circuit architecture in which parallel pathways carry distinct but complementary signals that jointly support visually evoked escape.

papers.title: Theta-band EEG changes following sequential rTMS and tACS in fibromyalgia: A randomized controlled pilot study
papers.abstract: Background: Sequential application of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) may induce neurophysiological changes within sensorimotor and pain-related networks. However, the resting-state EEG effects of this combined approach in fibromyalgia remain unknown. Methods: In this exploratory randomized controlled pilot study, 10 adults with fibromyalgia were assigned to active stimulation (n = 5) or a no-stimulation control group (n = 5). Active participants received one or two sessions of 10-Hz rTMS over the left primary motor cortex (1,000 pulses/session), followed by 10 daily sessions of bilateral 10-Hz tACS (1 mA, 20 min). Six-minute eyes-closed resting-state EEG recordings were obtained before and after the intervention or an equivalent control interval. Power spectral density was quantified in the delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands and analyzed using mixed repeated-measures ANOVAs across central-centroparietal and posterior regions of interest. Results: Theta power increased significantly in the active group but not in controls, yielding significant Time x Group (F(1,8)=8.70, p=.018, p2=.521) and Time x ROI x Group (F(1,8)=5.53, p=.047, p2=.409) interactions. Follow-up analyses showed increased theta power in both central-centroparietal (p=.004) and posterior (p=.012) regions, with a larger increase observed posteriorly. No significant interaction effects were found for delta, alpha, or beta power. Conclusions: Sequential motor-cortex rTMS followed by repeated bilateral 10-Hz tACS was associated with increased resting-state theta activity in fibromyalgia. Given the small sample size, post hoc ROI selection, lack of sham stimulation, and absence of component-specific control conditions, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require replication in adequately powered sham-controlled studies.

papers.title: Applications of functional ultrasound brain-computer interfaces in neurological diseases: research progress based on neurovascular coupling.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) bypass peripheral nerves and muscles to establish direct information pathways between the brain and external devices, providing novel approaches for motor function reconstruction, communication assistance, and neurorehabilitation in patients with neurological disorders. However, conventional non-invasive BCIs relying on modalities such as electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), or functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) exhibit limitations in spatiotemporal resolution, portability, or real-time capability. Functional ultrasound (fUS), an emerging neuroimaging technology based on neurovascular coupling (NVC), detects cerebral blood volume changes at a spatial resolution of approximately 100 μm; its imaging frame interval is 200-500 ms, whereas its effective temporal resolution, limited by the hemodynamic response, is 1-2 s, offering a potential solution to overcome these constraints. This review comprehensively analyzed NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces from the dimensions of technical principles, clinical applications, future directions, and challenges. fUS has demonstrated significant clinical value in stroke assessment, epilepsy monitoring, and early identification of neurodegenerative diseases. Emerging technologies such as transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation, sonogenetics, and intravascular ultrasound are driving the evolution of fUS from single-signal "acquisition" toward bidirectional "acquisition-modulation" closed-loop systems, which remain at the proof-of-concept stage. However, the hemodynamic response latency relative to neural electrical activity (1-2 s), the yet-unclear biosafety of chronic ultrasound exposure, and insufficient decoding reliability under pathological conditions remain critical bottlenecks requiring urgent resolution. In conclusion, NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces provide a novel tool for precision diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases. Future efforts should focus on conducting multicenter clinical trials and enhancing the robustness of decoding algorithms.

papers.title: Charitable giving with earned and windfall money: behavioral and ERP responses to donation-risk information.
papers.abstract: Charitable giving depends both on how money is acquired and on expectations about its eventual use. However, it remains unclear how monetary source shapes the evaluation of donation-risk information after a donation decision. Twenty-six participants made repeated donation decisions using earned and windfall money while electroencephalography was recorded. After each choice, a cue indicated a 70 % probability of allocation to either a lower-credibility charity (high risk) or a higher-credibility charity (low risk). One decision and its associated allocation rule were implemented at the end of the experiment. Participants donated more from windfall than earned money and reported greater regret and lower satisfaction after high-risk than low-risk cues. Mixed-effects analysis also showed lower next-trial donations following high-risk cues. Windfall money was associated with less positive frontocentral mean voltage within the feedback-related negativity (FRN) interval, whereas low-risk information elicited a larger P3. The predicted monetary-source-by-risk interaction was not supported, and Bayesian comparisons favored the zero-interaction model over the specified alternative. These findings show that monetary acquisition context and prospective allocation information both matter for charitable giving and its neural evaluation. They extend research on donation-related feedback by demonstrating behavioral adjustment to consequential risk information before the recipient and the realized charitable outcome are known.

papers.title: EEG monitoring in the neonate as part of a multimodal brain protection system in paediatric anaesthesia.
papers.abstract: Neurological monitoring is well established in anesthesia. Applied for assessment and control it also provides indirect information on hemodynamic status, ventilation, oxygenation and perfusion. In pediatric anesthesia, the potential toxicity of anesthetics is a concern. In neonates and young infants, the brain is immature and still developing, making electroencephalogram monitoring complex. To determine the current state of neurological function monitoring in neonates during anesthesia as a brain protection tool, a narrative review was conducted. The search prioritized the last ten years in PubMed, Cochrane, other electronic sources, and snowball sampling using the keywords: Neurotoxicity, Brain Monitoring, Newborn, Anesthesia, Neuroprotective Strategies, combinations thereof, and expert publications. The review concludes that brain protection is necessary, however further knowledge and validated technological support are required.

papers.title: Clinical meaning of significant intraindividual asymmetries in material-specific memory performance within the unimpaired range in 432 people with epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Material-specific memory deficits can provide lateralizing information regarding epileptogenic foci or structural lesions. Intraindividual performance asymmetries may occur despite overall unimpaired performance. This study investigates the clinical relevance of such asymmetries in people with epilepsy (PWE). We retrospectively analyzed data from 432 PWE who demonstrated unimpaired verbal and figural memory performance but exhibited significant intraindividual asymmetries in these domains, as determined by critical differences derived from co-normed data. Concordance between material-specific memory asymmetries and lateralization from MRI and EEG lateralization was evaluated using contingency tables and chi-square/Fisher's exact tests. Among 1,246 individuals with suspected epilepsy and unimpaired memory performance, 432 (34.7 %) with confirmed epilepsy diagnosis exhibited significant material-specific asymmetries. Of these, 367 (85.0 %) demonstrated a relative verbal memory superiority, and 65 (15.0 %) showed a figural memory superiority. Among PWE with lateralized temporal pathologies, Fisher's exact test showed a significant association between memory asymmetries and MRI lateralization, p = .036, V = .167. A chi-square test demonstrated no significant association between memory asymmetries and EEG lateralization, χ²(1) = 3.57, p = .059. No significant concordance emerged when temporal MRI and EEG findings were considered jointly, χ2(1) = 3.54, p = .060. The majority of PWE with significant intraindividual material-specific memory asymmetries within the unimpaired range exhibit verbal memory superiority. There is a statistically significant association of this performance asymmetry with MRI lateralization. In case of temporal pathologies, memory asymmetries clearly point to lateralized MRI pathologies, although the actual side cannot be reliably predicted due to putative reorganization processes.

papers.title: Elaborative processing before retrieval practice enhances semantic organization and long-term memory.
papers.abstract: One longstanding goal in psychology is to identify more effective ways of learning. Recent work has shown that elaborative processing can amplify the memory benefits of retrieval practice, yet the mechanisms underlying this advantage remain unclear. Using electroencephalography (EEG), the present study examined how elaborative processing before retrieval practice influences later memory and encoding-related neural processing and representations, relative to context processing. Behaviorally, memory performance was better for elaborative processing plus retrieval practice than for context processing plus retrieval practice. During the first encoding phase, elaborative processing elicited a more negative N400, whereas context processing elicited a more positive LPC. Moreover, the N400 and LPC differences between elaborative and context processing during encoding were significantly correlated with the corresponding differences in 7-day recognition performance. Representational similarity analyses further showed stronger semantic-category organization and greater representational reorganization across repeated encoding under elaborative processing than under context processing. These findings suggest that elaborative processing before retrieval practice enhances long-term memory and is associated with broader semantic processing and stronger semantic organization during encoding. More broadly, the results suggest that richer connections with pre-existing semantic knowledge may be one way in which encoding variability supports long-term memory.

papers.title: Making sense of touch: Spatial tactile cues promote efficient visuo-somatosensory integration and restore motor accuracy under sensory conflict.
papers.abstract: Effective interaction with complex environments relies on the integration of somatosensory and visual signals into coherent spatial representations of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, as during goal-directed hand movements under mirror-reversed visual feedback, motor performance deteriorates. Despite this conflict, the visual mapping between the hand and the environment remains preserved, and visual information typically facilitates motor performance, whereas tactile feedback impairs it. Here, we tested whether providing tactile input with explicit spatial structure renders visuo-somatosensory integration functionally relevant and stabilizes motor behaviour under sensory conflict. Healthy adults performed a mirror-tracing task, tracing a shape's contour with the index finger while tactile feedback conveyed either motion-related cues alone or additional discrete spatial landmarks aligned with the outline. Spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness relative to motion-related tactile input, indicating more effective online motor control. EEG source analyses further revealed that, when spatial tactile cues were present, somatosensory activity increased and functional connectivity was largely restricted to sensorimotor areas. In contrast, when tactile cues did not convey spatial information, sensory conflict was associated with widespread reductions in cortical activity, including in somatosensory and parietal areas, and with a diffuse functional connectivity pattern consistent with elevated sensorimotor uncertainty. Together, these findings indicate that providing spatial structure to tactile input can mitigate the detrimental effects of visuo-somatosensory conflict on motor performance and support more efficient integration of visual and somatosensory information during action. KEY POINTS: Accurate movements depend on combining visual and somatosensory information to estimate the position of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, motor performance usually deteriorates and tactile feedback can become disruptive. We tested whether tactile feedback becomes useful for movement control when it provides explicit spatial landmarks, rather than only motion-related information from finger-surface contact. During a tracing task under visuo-somatosensory conflict, spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness compared with when touch conveyed motion cues alone. papers.title: A mechanistic classification of GNAO1 mutations links Gβ γ sequestration to hyperkinetic disease and treatment response
papers.abstract: Go is the most prevalent G protein subunit in the brain and is critical for signal transduction through G protein-coupled receptors. Mutations in the gene encoding Go (GNAO1) cause a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements (NEDIM) and, in some patients, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). Here, we integrate human genetic analysis with cellular assays to define mechanistic classes of GNAO1 mutations and in vivo approaches to evaluate therapeutic strategies. We grouped variants into two functional categories: those predicted to sequester G{beta}{gamma} and those with reduced Go expression and therefore increased G{beta}{gamma} signaling. Analysis of patient data revealed that mutations predicted to impair G{beta}{gamma} release are significantly associated with NEDIM. Using the GNAO1R209H/+ mouse as a model of NEDIM, we evaluated two small molecules: caffeine, a nonselective adenosine receptor antagonist, and gallein, a selective modulator of G{beta}{gamma}-effector interactions. Both compounds significantly reduced hyperlocomotion in the open field test. Whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology revealed sex- and cell type-specific hyperexcitability in spiny projection neurons within the dorsolateral striatum of GNAO1R209H/+ mice. Together, these findings implicate dysfunction of dorsolateral striatal pathways in GNAO1-related disorder and suggest that mechanistic understanding of disease variants can guide targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Streamlined Production of Recombinant Adeno-Associated Viruses Using Gateway Cloning Technology for Neural Circuit All-Optical Interrogation
papers.abstract: The advent of optogenetics and the rapid development of genetically encoded actuators and reporters for calcium, voltage, neurotransmitters, and other molecules have revolutionized neuroscience research by enabling precise, non-invasive optical interrogation of neural circuits. Successful implementation, however, critically depends on efficient reporter expression in defined neuronal populations. We present a Gateway(R)-based cloning platform providing a robust pipeline for rapid, efficient construction of recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors optimized for neuroscience applications. This platform addresses promoter selection, indicator engineering, and capsid-type optimization, and enables systematic optimization of vector components across a range of optical tools. The benefit of this modular approach is illustrated in the case of ULoVE, a two-photon microscopy method based on acousto-optic deflectors (AODs). This method provides serial light-targeting with kHz sampling rates and high signal-to-noise ratio in vivo, which imposes stringent requirements on indicator expression -- including cell-type specificity, sparse labelling, and precise control of expression levels-- efficiently met through the combinatorial flexibility of the Gateway pipeline. As specific examples, Gateway-constructed Cre-driver viruses combined with Cre-dependent reporters enabled cell-type-specific labelling for two complementary applications. In cerebellar Purkinje cells, an L7::Cre driver virus paired with a Gateway-constructed voltage indicator (JEDI2P-Kv) and ULoVE two-photon excitation at ~5 kHz enables resolution of sub-millisecond dendritic voltage dynamics in awake, behaving mice, including optical detection of dendritic spikelets previously accessible only via intracellular electrophysiology. The same driver virus paired with calcium indicators (GCaMP6f, jRGECO1a) resolves climbing fiber-evoked calcium kinetics under the same conditions. In acute cerebellar slices, a kit::Cre driver virus enabled cell-type-specific expression of the optogenetic actuator ChR2(H134R) in molecular layer interneurons, where ULoVE doughnut-pattern photostimulation achieved single-cell, sub-millisecond optogenetic activation with micron-scale spatial resolution. Beyond ULoVE applications, the same sparse, strong labelling also proved suitable for anatomical tracing of axonal projections in cleared cerebellar tissue, resolving individual DCN axon terminals at the granule cell layer --molecular layer boundary. Taken together, our dual-front approach --combining a modular AAV expression pipeline with AOD-based optical acquisition --provides an integrated platform for developing sophisticated optical tools, including but not limited to AOD-based microscopy, for neural circuit interrogation.

papers.title: SCN2B Drives Depression-like Phenotypes in Mice by Suppressing BDNF Signaling via Its Intracellular Domain NICD.
papers.abstract: The rising global burden of depression necessitates novel mechanistic insights and therapeutic targets. Voltage-gated sodium channel β2-subunit (Navβ2, coded by SCN2B) has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders, yet its role in depression remains unexplored. Here, we identify SCN2B as a previously unrecognized driver of depression-like pathophysiology. Using SCN2B-overexpressing (SCN2B-OV) mice across different ages (1, 12, and 20 months) and CRISPR- engineered Navβ2V173A,V175K mice with selective reduction of the Navβ2 intracellular domain (NICD), we combined behavioral phenotyping, electrophysiology, neurotransmitter profiling, and molecular analyses, with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) as an environmental challenge. SCN2B-OV mice exhibited accelerated depression-like phenotypes, including anhedonia (sucrose preference 52.42% reduction, P<0.05), behavioral despair (forced swim test immobility 67.42% increase, P<0.05), and cognitive deficits (Y-maze alternation 50.90% reduction, P<0.05), independent of natural aging. Electrophysiologically, SCN2B overexpression induced a striking prefrontal-hippocampal imbalance: prefrontal cortex (PFC) became hyperexcitable (glutamate release increased by 64.7%; sEPSC amplitude increased 2.05-fold, P<0.05), whereas the hippocampus showed synaptic suppression (GABA release reduced by 32.65%; sIPSC frequency reduced by 66.67%, P<0.05). Mechanistically, SCN2B overexpression suppressed BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/AKT signaling axis (BDNF reduced by 53.17%; p-TrkB reduced by 63.62%, P<0.05), accompanied by decreased synaptic proteins (PSD95 43.45%, synapsin I 40.31%, P<0.05). Remarkably, NICD-reduced Navβ2V173A,V175K mice were fully resistant to CUMS-induced behavioral and neurotransmitter deficits, establishing NICD as a critical mediator of stress vulnerability. Collectively, these findings unravel a causal pathway in which SCN2B overexpression drives NICD-dependent suppression of BDNF signaling, leading to region-specific excitatory/inhibitory imbalance, synaptic disintegration, and depression-like phenotypes. Targeting Navβ2 proteolysis to block NICD generation may thus represent a novel therapeutic strategy for mood disorders.

The combination of 800 μg/mL RELGGFF and 50 mg/mL oat β-glucan produced the strongest synergistic effect, achieving an enzyme inhibition rate of 71.14 ± 1.52% and a combination index (CI) value of 0.71. Molecular docking and spectral analysis indicated that RELGGFF and oat β-glucan could tightly bind to α-glucosidase and synergistically inhibit its activity by influencing its conformational stability. This study established a theoretical foundation for the synergistic application of RELGGFF and oat β-glucan in the management of type 2 diabetes (T2D).

papers.title: Optical, Morphology, and Structural Characterization of Synthesized Eco-Friendly Silver Nanoparticles for Potential Antibacterial Applications.
papers.abstract: In this work, the silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were synthesized by an eco-friendly biosynthesis using Bougainvillea spectabilis leaf extract, which acts as reducing and capping agent. The AgNPs were analyzed using UV spectroscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, XRD, and scanning electron SEM. From the UV-visible spectral analysis we recorded an SPR peak at 415 nm, which is characteristic of spherical AgNPs. The results obtained from FTIR suggest the potential role of biomolecules in reducing Ag+ and the capping of AgNPs. The XRD pattern demonstrated the FCC crystalline of metallic silver, showing average crystallite size ranging from 30 to 50 nm. Results obtained from the SEM revealed the morphology and size distribution of synthesized AgNPs. From the images obtained, we determined a spherical morphology with an estimated size distribution measuring 50-200 nm. Furthermore, the AgNPs exhibited strong antibacterial behavior against tested bacterial strains, namely Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These results highlight that the silver NPs are sustainable for potential biomedical and environmental applications.
